items.title: George Guesnon Interview
items.q: if I wanted to know something on the banjo, I'd ask people like Kimball and Sales.

ctx.x: If I remember rightly now, it's coming to me a little bit. It seems like you said once, Glennie said, if you're going to ask somebody, don't ask a damn fool the question. Oh, yeah.

Oh, yeah. Always. No, that's what he said. He said, every man can be taught something by somebody. But just so the man is not a damn fool. That's all. He said, make sure when you go to a man to ask him concerning something that the man is able to tell you what to do. And he's right. You understand? That's right. In other words, if I wanted to know something on the banjo, I'd ask people like Kimball and Sales. You understand what I mean? I wouldn't ask Black Walter because he wouldn't know. He's my friend and all,…
Yes, very good. All right, let's see. Can you tell us a little bit more about your first days? How long did you stay there at the Hummingbird, and where did you go after that?
